title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-taylor-cho
content:
PR: runtime/pull/1234 — kv-cache + batching refactor (WIP)

Quick summary:
- Large refactor to kv cache ownership and continuous batching pipeline. Goal: reduce mutex contention, allow per-model cache lifetimes, and enable adaptive batch sizing.
- Adds CacheManager abstraction, moves cache eviction to background worker, and introduces BatchScheduler that predicts optimal batch size based on recent latency/throughput signals.

High-level review checklist (my notes while reading):
- [ ] Correctness: ensure no staleness or incorrect KV reuse across requests/models. Look for model_id scoping and cache keys.
- [ ] Concurrency: are locks minimized? verify no double-checked locking bugs.
- [ ] Memory safety: cache lifecycle + background eviction should not reference freed model state.
- [ ] Metrics/observability: new components should emit latency, hit/miss, and memory usage metrics.
- [ ] Tests: unit tests + integration + fuzzing for race conditions.
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: rolling restart plan, migration for existing cached entries.

Notes on files changed (scan highlights):
- cache/manager.py: new CacheManager class. Looks clean but missing explicit null-check when model teardown happens (line ~248). Potential race: background eviction may call _evict(model_id) while ModelSession is shutting down. Add a guard or weakref.
- batch/scheduler.py: added predictive algorithm using EWMA on token latencies. Algorithm seems okay but hyperparams are hard-coded. Suggest wiring to runtime/config or expose as feature flags for experiments.
- serving/request_handler.py: switched to use CacheManager.get_or_populate(...). There is a short window where a request may see an empty cache and trigger two concurrent populates — the CacheManager currently uses a per-key lock, but the lock granularity is coarse (per-model). Consider per-key/per-prefix locks to reduce contention for hot models.

Concrete issues to address before merge:
1) Race during model teardown: add model_exists_check in CacheManager._evict and also in background worker loop; fallback to noop if model gone. Add unit test simulating rapid load/unload.
2) Deduplicate concurrent populates: implement singleflight-style inflight map keyed by (model_id, prefix_hash) to avoid duplicate loads. Tests: assert only one populate call for concurrent requests.
3) BatchScheduler hyperparams: move to config with sensible defaults and add a small integration test that validates behavior under synthetic latency distributions.
4) Metrics: add CacheManager.* metrics: cache_hit_total, cache_miss_total, cache_size_bytes, cache_evictions_total, batch_size_chosen. Hook them into existing prometheus registry.
5) Logging: too many DEBUG logs in the hot path (batching decisions). Reduce log level or sample.

Testing plan suggestions:
- Unit tests for CacheManager eviction, populate dedupe, and teardown guards.
- Integration test: spin up a minimal runtime instance with 3 worker threads, load model A, send heavy concurrent requests with prefix collisions and assert correct behavior (no duplicate populates, memory stabilizes).
- Load test: run perf harness (use existing perf/bench scripts) to verify throughput gains and that latency SLOs remain met at 95/99 percentiles.

Design/behavioral questions for author (leave as comments in PR):
- Why chose per-model lock instead of per-key? tradeoffs? was it to control memory and lock map size?
- How does adaptive batch size interact with autoscaling? Could aggressive batching starve CPU/GPU resources?
- Eviction policy: LRU vs TTL vs combined. Current impl uses TTL; is there workload data supporting TTL-only?

Refactor suggestions / improvements:
- Lightweight singleflight to dedupe populates (low-risk, high-reward).
- Replace coarse locks with sharded lock map (e.g., 256 shards) to reduce contention without unbounded lock map growth.
- Expose BatchScheduler hyperparams via Config and add an experimentation switch to enable predictive mode.
- Add a small README under cache/ explaining invariants (ownership, lifecycle) to prevent future regressions.

Follow-ups / action items (for PR author or me to do after merge):
- [ ] Author: address teardown race + add tests.
- [ ] Author: implement inflight dedupe or clearly document why not.
- [ ] Me: run local perf tests once unit tests green and post results in PR comment thread.
- [ ] Me: add a canary rollout doc for Dedicated deployments — how to safely roll this change (gradual model-by-model rollout, monitor cache evictions and memory). Link to rollout checklist in Confluence.

Acceptance criteria for merge:
- Tests covering teardown race and singleflight behavior added and passing.
- No performance regression on synthetic benchmark (95th p95 <= baseline * 1.05).
- Metrics instrumented and dashboards created (or tickets created to add dashboards).
- Author addressed the logging spam in hot path.

Quick TODOs to add as comments in the PR (inline):
- Line 112 in cache/manager.py: add "if model_id not in model_registry: return"
- Line 205 in request_handler.py: replace model-level lock with lock_for(prefix_hash) or add TODO to explain decision
- batch/scheduler.py: move EWMA alpha to CONFIG and add comment about units

Misc notes / thoughts to self:
- This change could substantially reduce token cost if cache hit rate rises for multi-turn sessions. Worth running an economics check: simulate per-request token savings vs extra CPU usage from background eviction.
- Might be a good candidate for Redwood Optimize guidance (generate recommended TTLs + batching profiles automatically).

Slack threads to reference in PR comments:
- #eng-runtime — thread: "kv-cache refactor initial perf" (link: slack-thread/abc123)
- #sre — notes about memory alarms when background evictions spike (thread: slack-thread/mem-evict-45)

Estimated review time: 2-3 hours (deep read + run tests).

If I have time today: run the unit tests locally, add the singleflight change as a small separate commit, and document the rollout plan.

End of scratchpad.
